title: minimal 1D transposed convolutions

atoms.evidence: x_mod = pad1d(x, left=kernel_width - 1, right=kernel_width - 1, pad_value=0); weights_mod = einops.rearrange(weights.flip(-1), 'i o w -> o i w'); return conv1d_minimal(x_mod, weights_mod) — exact 'pad by (k-1) then flip kernel then conv' identity

einops.rearrange(weights.flip(-1), 'i o w -> o i w') — explicit (in, out, k) -> (out, in, k) axis swap after flip; markdown: 'in our convolutions we assumed the kernel had shape (out_channels, in_channels, kernel_width). Here, the order is different: in_channels comes before out_channels'
pad1d(x, left=kernel_width - 1, right=kernel_width - 1, pad_value=0) — zero-padding by (k-1) on each side; the part2 pad1d primitive reused directly
return conv1d_minimal(x_mod, weights_mod) — the part2 conv1d_minimal (as_strided windowing) is the actual workhorse

notes: 4 atoms — slightly under seed prediction of 5. The introduction to transposed convolutions: introduces the two §6 atoms convT-as-flipped-padded-conv and convT-kernel-axis-swap together. Reuses pad1d (conv-padding-zero) and conv1d_minimal (conv-windowing-1d) from part2 — clean 4-atom implementation of the foundational convT identity.
